# Continue the existing avatar request without duplicate submission

This later CF-08 recovery addendum supersedes only OWNER.md's instruction to start
a new edit. Preserve that original brief, src/avatar.ts, input.png and reference.png.
The existing consumer expects a 32x32 PNG at assets/robot.png. These images and the
provider are controlled fixtures, not real PixelLab generation or human acceptance.

The saved store is .pixl/recovery. Job recoverable-job has a lost submission response; recover it
using exact originating-connection observations. Job unresolved-job is a separate
unknown attempt with insufficient observations; absence in a listing cannot prove
non-acceptance. Keep that job unknown unless actual matching evidence resolves it.
There is no authorization for a new request, paid or simulated. Do not dispatch,
prepare, generate, upload, replace provider identity or abandon unknown work to
bypass it. Original local journal/state evidence remains immutable.

Use ordinary jobs/workflow reports, job-observe and job-import. Read the installed
shared skill/profile and provider-recovery reference; use actual tool schemas/help.
Choose the correct current expected hash for each mutation. Provider success is
not complete retrieval, and imported bytes are not visual/engine acceptance.
Do not fabricate candidate reviews, nominate, complete tasks or alter criteria.

The experiment has three separately launched artifact-recovery phases. A fresh
caller and named child consume the SAME root/store/kit each round; these are not
same-session or same-child native continuations. Follow only the assigned phase.
Phase1 reconciles identity, observes progress and preserves the interrupted HTTP
retrieval as a useful partial handoff. Phase2 cold-recovers complete bytes/imports
and gives the caller a useful file. Phase3 cold-consumes that exact retained
candidate and confirms current state without another dispatch or import.

Caller: delegate to the actual named specialist, supply this root, kit, Python and
phase assignment, retain its real child ID and wait for its result. Codex uses
agent_type='pixl', fork_turns='none'. Do not substitute a generic child. Independently
read the specialist's exact report and current jobs/state, inspect actual returned
files/diagnostics and verify src/avatar.ts's path mapping. Report partial recovery
honestly; do not require unrelated artistic or human acceptance for this assignment.

All new work belongs under work/provider-recovery/phase-N or this existing .pixl/recovery; assets/robot.png
may first be created in phase2 as an exact byte copy, clearly unaccepted for art.
Keep earlier phase files unchanged. Retain actual stdout/errors rather than making
up observations. Capture timestamps from the clock when needed, never from memory.

---
name: pixl

For an assigned pixel-art production task, adopt the [PIXL profile](../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). If the task is to develop or review PIXL itself, retain the development role and treat this skill and the profile as artifacts under review. Merely reading their instructions does not change the reader's role. Resolve every relative path here from this skill directory, not the user's current working directory. The plugin root is two directories above this file's directory. Read only resources needed for the current operation.

Start with [everyday asset production](references/everyday.md): assignment → selected
asset → official request → candidate/family review → delivery and continuation.
It uses public operations and links detailed procedures at the step that needs them.
For another consumer or uncertain host/tool setup, use [observed readiness](references/readiness.md)
to distinguish installed files, actual specialist/local-tool access and the
official provider connection. Continue established work when access is already known.
Use [hash identities and paths](references/identities-and-paths.md) when choosing a
publication guard, following a source locator, exporting a result or relocating a

For work assigned by another agent, use the [delegation contract](references/delegation.md) to carry project context and return consumable results. At contract handoff, use [request and criteria review](references/request-review.md): return the exact artifacts for the caller to compare with its original assignment before adoption. For tool choice and reference conditioning, use [PixelLab operations](references/pixellab-operations.md). Start from the official [platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs); then inspect the relevant connected tool declaration.

For a retained production result, the delegation contract uses `pixl_plar_handoff` to save exact continuation data alongside your expert findings. Choose `view: "caller"` (CLI `--view caller`) for the [compact caller result](../../resources/spec/caller-result.md), with authored findings separate from derived state and exact full retrievals. Return its handoff path/hash so another agent can resume without a manually rewritten job summary.

The [state-authority reference](references/state-authority.md) preserves the detailed production-state rules. Load it when authoring or resuming state. PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.

Read [the artistic-authority checks](references/artistic-authority.md) when deriving aesthetic restrictions or auditing a contradictory approach; the retained examples are conditional guidance.

Use [isolated consumer execution](references/consumer-execution.md) when the actual consumer implements the shipped queue-motion profile. It retains exact delivered files, observed frames/wraps and reduced-motion switches without hand-written launch logic; visual judgment and acceptance remain explicit.

Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.

Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.

Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.

The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.

The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.

Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.

Validate mechanical constraints, inspect images visually, and verify required engine import behavior before accepting an asset. Report what was checked and what remains uncertain. Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. `pixl_commit` accepts a JSON `document` directly or a `candidate` wire-file path; both use the same validation. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.

# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
changing the user's global configuration.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
without manufacturing PLAR or production records:

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
not automatically summarized.

For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:

```json
{
  "status": "partial",
  "caller": {
    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
    "integration": {
      "status": "not_performed",
      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
    },
    "issues": [
      {
        "category": "unfinished_work",
        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.

Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.
# Provider submission and recovery operation

Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.

Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.

## Required context

- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.

Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.

## Prepare a saved request

Prefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging. Preserve image transport identifiers with their local source hashes. The optional HTTP route below is a selected integration, not a substitute for every MCP workflow.

When the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`
to inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.
It currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,
not live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.
`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task
and output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;
do not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once
(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`
decodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation
requires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.
Unknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.
Mocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.

1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Capture observation time from the host clock when observing/recording the response (for example, Python datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()); keep provider event time separate. Do not invent a precise time from the session date, and omit optional timestamps that were not observed. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.

Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.

## Claim once, then call the actual provider

Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.

The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.

Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.

# Provider recovery journal version 1

This is the normative external-file contract for the opt-in [PX2 durable J](PIXL-2.md) extension. Files are UTF-8 canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, no ASCII escaping, finite values) followed by one LF. Hashes are SHA-256 of exact bytes unless described as a canonical JSON value hash (which omits the final LF). Every object has closed fields; arbitrary supplied evidence and argument values remain bounded JSON objects.

The top-level fields are `version` (integer 1), `intent`, `intent_sha256` (canonical value hash of intent), `events`, `state`, `remote_id`. Intent has `job` (PIXL identifier), `request`, `context`. Context has `task`, distinct nonempty `outputs`, `task_sha256` and `bindings` (record IDs to hashes, including every output). Task hash covers its record without mutable st/ca/vr. Bindings cover selected outputs and the semantic closure of task inputs, decisions and methods. Context is immutable after preparation.

Request fields are `version` (1), `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `schema_sha256`, `request_sha256`, `discovery`, `authorization`, `prepared_at`, `policy` (`caller_schema`), `remote_executed` (false), `cached_assessment`. Request hash covers the provider/tool/arguments/schema object. The exact supplied schema governs argument validation. Discovery has source, observed_at and nonempty evidence. Authorization has scope and nonempty evidence. Dates are ISO timestamps. Provider/tool/source/scope are nonempty strings. These are caller assertions; they neither authenticate a remote service nor grant additional authority.

New request preparation rejects a discovery observation later than the local preparation clock. This check applies before publishing new intent; existing version-1 histories retain their original caller assertions and remain readable without rewriting their bytes.

Cached assessment is a retained advisory result, never recomputed to reinterpret old intent. It has advisory=true, source, retrieved_at, status and findings. Status describes passed/conflict/unlisted/unavailable/not_applicable; findings contain code/detail. A caller-schema-valid request may report a cache conflict without rewriting arguments or claiming the cache is current. Credential fields in supplied values are rejected. This is a field-name guard, not detection of every secret that could be embedded in prose.

Each event has `sequence` (1-based contiguous integer), `event`, `recorded_at`, `remote_id`, nonempty `evidence`, and `artifact`. Artifact is null except for imported, where it has `id`, `output`, `record_sha256`. The candidate ID is unique in the journal, and output must belong to intent. State and identity are derived by replay; they cannot be edited independently. All request and event timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and support at most six fractional-second digits. Event instants cannot run backward or precede preparation; different offset spellings of the same instant are permitted. Unsupported precision is rejected without truncation. Evidence remains caller-supplied data.

Dispatch occurs once from prepared, has no remote ID and yields unknown. Before dispatch, only failed may abandon preparation. After dispatch, submitted/running/unknown observations may repeat; running cannot regress to submitted, including through unknown. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require an observed ID.
